html:
The Hippodamian grid plan is the layout of a city in straight streets crossing at right angles, named after Hippodamus of Miletus, a Greek planner of the 5th century BCE.

Hippodamus laid out Piraeus, the harbour town of Athens, in the time of Pericles. He is said to have planned Thurii in southern Italy too. Aristotle wrote that he was the first person to theorise about how a city should be arranged, dividing it into zones for temples, public life and homes.

He did not invent the grid. Greek colonies had used rectangular plans since the 8th century BCE, and Miletus was rebuilt on a grid after the Persians destroyed it in 494 BCE. But his name stuck to the idea. Later cities built by Alexander and his successors, such as Alexandria, used it, and so did Roman camps and towns. Many colonial cities of the modern world were laid out the same way.
sum: The Hippodamian grid plan is the layout of a city in straight streets crossing at right angles, named after Hippodamus of Miletus, a Greek planner of the 5th century BCE.
